results.name: Snake Path, 1992
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Alexis Smith's Snake Path uses pointed allusions to the biblical conflict between innocence and knowledge, and marks an apt symbolic path to the university's main repository of books. Ends at the terrace of Geisel Library URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/AlexisSmith.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Two Running Violet V Forms, 1983
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Robert Irwin's piece comprises "fences" of blue-violet fencing contrasting with the ordered eucalyptus grove surrounding the piece. Eucalyptus groves east of the Mandeville Center and adjacent to the Faculty Club URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Irwin.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: La Jolla Vista View, 1988
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: La Jolla Vista View, William Wegman's only major outdoor permanent sculpture, includes a long bronze map, telescope, drinking fountain and picnic table, creating an overlook near UCSD's theatre district. Near the theater complex URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Wegman.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Standing, 1998
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Set in the School of Medicine, Kiki Smith's Standing illustrates her vision of the human body as a fluid vehicle for intimating life and death. The Madonna-like figure perched atop a tree trunk calls forth thoughts of human strength and frailty.   Between the Basic Science and Medical Teaching buildings URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/KikiSmith.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Green Table, 1992
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Jenny Holzer's Green Table serves as an informal gathering place for students and faculty to eat, study or play. Engraved with her humorous and sometimes politically charged writings, it creates a site for questioning and debate. Muir College Quad URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Holzer.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Trees, 1986
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Artist Terry Allen created this piece in which three trees, salvaged from a eucalyptus grove cleared for construction, were encased in lead. "Trees" symbolizes the displacement and loss of the natural environment of UCSD. Eucalyptus grove between Geisel Library and the Faculty Club URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Allen.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Untitled, 1991
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Juxtaposed with a large American flag and WWII commemorative plaque and set in front of UCSD's main administrative complex, Michael Asher's granite drinking fountain Untitled suggests the continuity between the institutions of defense and learning. Myers Drive, across from the Chancellors Complex URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Asher.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: READ/WRITE/THINK/DREAM, 2001
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: This piece by John Baldessari at the entrance to the Geisel Library comprises a wall of 8 10-foot-high glass panels flanking two pairs of automatic sliding doors, replaced with glass in primary colors. Geisel Library main entrance URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Baldessari.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Bear, 2005
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Bear, artist Tim Hawkinson's 2005 contribution to the Stuart Collection, stands over 23 feet high and is made of uncut granite boulders. This enormous stone teddy bear is surrounded by the high-tech buildings of the Engineering School. Academic courtyard, Jacobs School of Engineering URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Hawkinson.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Terrace, 1991
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Jackie Ferrara has designed and built courtyards, terraces, and architectural structures since the early 1970s. Cellular and Molecular Medicine Facility URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Ferrara.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Vices and Virtues, 1988
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Bruce Nauman's Vices and Virtues consists of 7 pairs of words superimposed in blinking colored neon, running around the top of the Powell Structure Systems Laboratory. Warren College URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Nauman.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Another, 2008
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: The mural on the large interior wall of the main space depicts a double image of clocks, news ticker, and is punctuated by phrases indicating "another" aspect of life. The piece suggests how our lives are culturally inflected, constructed and contained. Price Center East, west interior wall URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Kruger.htm

results.name: UNDA, 1987
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Ian Hamilton Finlay created a one-word poem using the four letters UNDA (Latin for "wave") and the editor's wave-shaped mark used to transpose these letters. The five limestone blocks, previously installed at one edge of the north playing field in Marshall College, are now located at the south field by Rady School of Management.  Learn more: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Finlay.htm

results.name: What Hath God Wrought, 2018
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Artist: Mark BradfordLocation: Revelle PlazaThe 199-foot tall metal flag-pole-like sculpture—now considered the tallest structure on the University’s campus—is mounted with a flashing light which playfully spells out “What Hath God Wrought” in Morse Code. The titular phrase is notably the first message Samuel Morse tested and transmitted across 41-miles, over the communication system he’d newly designed with partner Alfred Vail, from Baltimore to Washington in 1844.Learn more: https://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/artist/bradford.html

results.name: The Wind Garden, 2017
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: The Wind Garden (2017) is a sound work by the composer John Luther Adams located in the historic Eucalyptus grove immediately west of the theaters. A continually changing series of harmonic tones are generated by the movement of trees in the wind, influenced by daily and annual positions of the sun.

results.name: La Jolla Project, 1984
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Richard Fleischner's La Jolla Project comprises 71 blocks of pink and gray granite arranged in configurations that refer to architectural vocabulary, transforming an ordinary lawn into a space reminiscent of an ancient ruin or construction site. Revelle College lawn, south of Galbraith Hall URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Fleischner.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Something Pacific, 1986
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: In Nam June Paik's Something Pacific, old and disintegrating televisions and Buddhas are embedded in the landscape outside of a lobby displaying a lively interactive bank of TV monitors. Lobby of the Media Center URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Paik.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Fallen Star, 2011
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: The little blue house and rooftop garden of Do Ho Suh's Fallen Star sit atop Jacobs Hall overlooking Warren Mall in the Jacobs School of Engineering. 7th floor roof of Jacobs Hall overlooking Warren Mall, JSOE, between the Bioengineering Building and head of the Snake Path. 9500 Gilman Drive, MC 0403 URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/artists/suh.shtml

results.name: Red Shoe, 1996
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Elizabeth Murray's giant Red Shoe lopes its way through one of UCSD's many eucalyptus groves, evoking thoughts of childhood play, nursery rhymes and fairytales. Eucalyptus trees near the theater complex URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Murray.htm (858) 534-2117

results.name: Sun God, 1983
results.subtitle: Art - Stuart Collection
results.description: Niki De Saint Phalle's Sun God was the first work commissioned by the Stuart Collection. The exuberantly colored, fourteen-foot bird is sited on a grassy area between the Faculty Club and Mandeville Auditorium. Sun God has become a landmark on campus.   On a grassy area between the Faculty Club and Mandeville Auditorium URL: http://stuartcollection.ucsd.edu/StuartCollection/Phalle.htm (858) 534-2117

results.description: RIMAC field sits below the recreation facility and is used for competition and training fields. Approximately 30% of campus irrigation uses recycled water.
